World: org A, with T1 and T2 in BU a1 and T3 in BU a2. T2 is moved to phase design / status active by a fixture update, with its audit event.

(b) For every caller, both units, and five phase/status combinations: take the ids the client's source list (GET /transformations?businessUnitId&phase&status) offers, and send them with the same phase and status to all three reads. Expect 200, rows within the list, and no other T id outside appliedFilters.
(c) Forged id lists (unreadable, other-BU, other-org, unknown, mixed with readable ones) × four phase/status combinations: expect 404 on all three reads.
(d) For an unreadable id against an unknown id, the 404 bodies must be identical (no existence oracle).

(b) 63 list→read requests: every offered id is accepted (200), rows ⊆ list, 0 leaks. For example, TL1 sees only T1, office sees T1,T2 in a1 and T3 in a2, and AUD narrows correctly. leadA1, ADM and OUT get an empty list, so the client sends no read.

(e) The org-wide rows equal the readable set narrowed by phase and status for TL1, TL2, TL3, FIN1 and AUD. ADM-only and OUT get 404 on all three reads.

checks_run.procedure:
Reproduce deterministically the unit failure seen in 3 of 5 full runs, F-DG4-106.
- Append probes/sec-dg4-r5-y1c-timing.append.tsx (sha256 ebc53171…) to an unchanged copy of apps/web/src/auth/session-bound.test.tsx, in the probe clone only (removed afterwards).
- It runs Y1c unchanged, except that one answer (selected by regex) is held for 2.2 s once the POST is sent, using the spec's own hold().
- Six variants: detail GET, /summary, /audit, /decisions, /me, POST.
checks_run.command: Y1C_HOLD='<regex>' pnpm exec vitest run --project unit-web src/auth/zz-sec-r5-y1c.test.tsx -t SEC-DG4-R5 (six variants)
checks_run.environment: Node 22.22.2, probe clone $TMPDIR/probe at e29a735.
checks_run.expected: If the extra /me is the designed 2 s identity re-check (client.ts:232, D-077), delaying one page-load answer past 2 s yields 3 /me and fails Y1c's exact count of 2.
checks_run.actual:
Exit 1 by design.

When the /summary, /audit or POST answer is held 2.2 s, the sequence after the POST shows a third GET /me before the next page GET, and Y1c's 'toHaveLength(2)' fails with 3. For /summary the sequence is '… GET /…/summary | GET /…/audit | GET /me | GET /decisions…'.

When the detail GET, the /decisions GET or the /me answer is held, the count is 2 and the test passes: those GETs were sent within the window.

The product behaves as designed (a page GET more than 2 s after the last /me revalidates identity first), and every identity guarantee of the spec holds. The defect is the test's exact count under wall-clock timing. I raise it as F-DG4-106: Low, not mandatory, owner frontend-ux-engineer. It does not block.
